title: auth: clarify header semantics for project/org keys, scoped tokens, CORS, and request signing
author: Asha Patel
description:
Motivation: multiple clients (OpenAI-compat wrappers, internal services, and third-party integrations) have inconsistent assumptions about which headers carry authentication and how cross-origin responses surface auth details. We need a single, well-documented header semantics model that: 1) preserves OpenAI compatibility for 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' clients, 2) clearly separates org-level keys from project-scoped keys, 3) introduces a small, opt-in request signing/nonce flow to mitigate replay for high-sensitivity endpoints, and 4) fixes CORS exposures so browser SDKs can surface token metadata safely.

Summary of changes: consolidated auth header handling in proxy layer, introduced explicit scoped token header and request signing headers, exposed minimal auth metadata in CORS and added clear deprecation paths for legacy headers. The change implements the following behavior: 
- Continue to accept Authorization: Bearer <token> for backwards compatibility. If token is an org key (prefix org_), treat as organization-scoped: can access cross-project resources in same org. If token is a project key (prefix proj_), treat as project-scoped: limited to resources in that project.
- New header X-Redwood-Scoped-Token: preferred for SDKs that want to indicate explicit project-scoped tokens; when present it takes precedence over Authorization for project-scoped auth. This helps disambiguate client intent and is useful for server-side routing.
- New request signing headers: X-RW-Req-Nonce and X-RW-Req-Signature. Nonce is a short random string, Signature is HMAC-SHA256(nonce + body) using a signing key derived from the provided token. This is optional and gated behind a runtime flag 'enable_req_signing' and will be used initially for the /v1/private/* admin endpoints.
- CORS: added Access-Control-Expose-Headers: X-Redwood-Scopes, X-Redwood-Project, X-RW-Auth-Warning. We avoid exposing raw tokens. We added Access-Control-Allow-Credentials behavior notes in docs for browser SDKs.
- OpenAI compatibility: the /v1/openai-compat layer remains accepting Authorization header. Added a compatibility shim to populate X-Redwood-Project from openai-compatible "OpenAI-Project" query param when present to preserve behavior from older clients that encoded project selection there.

Files/areas changed (high-level): consolidated logic into go/proxy/auth/headers.go and go/proxy/auth/validate.go; compatibility layer in redwood-openai-compat/handler.go; docs updated at docs/api/auth.md and docs/migrations/auth-headers.md; types and SDK notes in redwood-sdk-typescript/README-auth.md.

Migration notes: server-side effects are backward compatible. Projects using Authorization: Bearer continue to work. We recommend SDKs adopt X-Redwood-Scoped-Token to make intent explicit. Request signing is opt-in; no legacy clients required changes. We add a runtime feature-flag for gradual rollout.

Testing: unit tests for header precedence and token parsing added in go/proxy/auth/headers_test.go; integration tests for CORS exposures in integration/cors_test.go; e2e with openai-compat in perf-canary configured. CI passes locally and on CI after a flake was addressed.

Rollout: gated by feature flag 'enable_req_signing' and 'expose_auth_metadata' with a canary rollout to Dedicated and Hosted clusters; no DB migrations.

Related: ENG-2742 (design doc), SUP-4321 (customer incident that motivated nonce flow), redwood-sdk-typescript#121 (follow-up SDK change).

Checklist:
- [x] Design doc linked (ENG-2742)
- [x] Unit & integration tests
- [x] Docs updated
- [x] Feature flags for rollout

If merged: add a brief note to the 2025-02 platform changelog and ping SDK owners for coordinated minor releases.

release_notes: Clarified Authorization header semantics: org_ vs proj_ token prefixes, introduced X-Redwood-Scoped-Token as preferred header for project-scoped tokens, opt-in request signing headers X-RW-Req-Nonce and X-RW-Req-Signature, CORS exposure fixes. Backwards compatible; SDKs should migrate to scoped header where possible.
